---
title: "stokesjx"
subtitle: "Instantaneous viscous response of a spherically symmetric mantle to internal loads (geoid, dynamic topography, surface velocity), in JAX, with derivatives"
---

## What this code does

`stokesjx` computes the instantaneous viscous (Stokes) response of a spherically
symmetric, self-gravitating mantle to internal density anomalies.

- **Kernels.** For each spherical-harmonic degree `l` and each source radius, the package
  computes four kernels. They are the geoid, the dynamic topography of the surface and of
  the core-mantle boundary (CMB), and the surface velocity.
- **Fields.** A field is the radial integral of a kernel times a density anomaly. The
  package also gives the free-air gravity anomaly and the admittance from the field
  coefficients.
- **Derivatives.** Every step is written in JAX. The kernels and the fields have
  derivatives with respect to the layer viscosities and the radii of movable viscosity
  boundaries. Every leaf of the radial profile has a derivative too. The derivatives are for Hamiltonian
  Monte Carlo (HMC) over the radial viscosity.
- **Scope.** The package gives values and derivatives only. It does not choose a
  sampler or a prior.

## The method

`stokesjx` is a propagator method in the variable `ln r`. For each degree, two sweeps of
a three-vector basis run through the mantle, one upward from the CMB and one downward
from the surface. After each interval the basis is orthonormalised. Each sweep therefore
stays well conditioned, and the method is stable in float64 at every degree.

The Fortran code CODE-A multiplies the propagators of all intervals into one product.
That product holds the growing and the decaying solutions together, and their ratio over
the mantle is about $(R/r_c)^{2l+3}$, with $R = 6370$ km and $r_c = 3480$ km. This ratio
is 2e11 at `l = 20` and 1e27 at `l = 50`, so CODE-A needs 128-bit reals. `stokesjx` needs
no 128-bit reals. [The physics page](physics.qmd) gives the equations and the method.

## Who wrote the original

**Siavash Ghelichkhan** wrote and developed CODE-A at Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität
München (2016). The method of CODE-A comes from Corrieu, Thoraval and Ricard (1995) and
Hager and Clayton (1989). The compressible terms come from Forte and Peltier (1991), and
the propagator formulation from Ricard, Fleitout and Froidevaux (1984) and Richards and
Hager (1984).

Parts of `stokesjx` are ported from lovejx (Siavash Ghelichkhan, Jerry X. Mitrovica,
William Scott and Mark Hoggard). These parts are the layer parameterisation of the
controls, the integration of gravity, the pattern of the unit scales, the
spherical-harmonic conventions and the Taylor-test policy. CODE-A uses the quad-precision LINPACK routines
of John Burkardt. The Fortran is not distributed with `stokesjx`.

::: {.callout-note}
## How to cite

Cite the method:

Corrieu, V., Thoraval, C. and Ricard, Y. (1995). Mantle dynamics and geoid Green
functions. *Geophysical Journal International*, **120**, 516-523.

Hager, B. H. and Clayton, R. W. (1989). Constraints on the structure of mantle
convection using seismic observations, flow models, and the geoid. In *Mantle
Convection: Plate Tectonics and Global Dynamics*, ed. W. R. Peltier, Gordon and Breach,
657-763.

Cite the software by its repository, <https://github.com/g-adopt/stokesjx>. The
repository has no `CITATION.cff` yet ([open points](open-points.qmd)).
:::

## Validation

Three independent references check the values:

| Reference | Bound | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| CODE-A golden output under CODE-A's own switches, all 50 degrees | `1e-12` | 2.7e-14 (hager4), 1.8e-13 (smooth viscosity) |
| A second solver in mpmath at 50 to 250 digits, degrees 1 to 200 | `1e-12` | at most 8.5e-14 on the moderate cases |
| Analytical solutions of Kramer, Davies and Wilson (2021) through `assess` | `1e-12` | 1.2e-14 |

[The validation page](validation.qmd) gives the detail, and [the open
points](open-points.qmd) state what is not checked yet.

## Install

Install the package from a source checkout:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/g-adopt/stokesjx
cd stokesjx
pip install -e ".[test]"
```

[The install page](install.qmd) gives the other extras and the test run.

## Agentic coding

Agentic coding tools wrote this software under the direction and review of the author.
[The agentic-coding page](agentic-coding.qmd) states what the tools wrote, what the
author decided, and which checks the result must pass.
